question.text: Mr. Vikram Rao, Head of Distribution at 'Satpura AIF', is approached by a prospective LP who asks about 'pass-back' arrangements to sweeten subscriptions. Under SEBI (Prohibition of Fraudulent and Unfair Trade Practices) Regulations, 2003, which of the following is TRUE?

answer.text: Pass-backs (indirect incentives to induce subscriptions) and soft-dollar arrangements with distributors are prohibited; assuring returns is also prohibited. AIFs and distributors must observe high standards of ethics, integrity and fairness
Pass-backs are permitted if disclosed in the PPM and capped at 1% of subscription amount
Pass-backs are permitted only to Accredited Investors
Soft-dollar arrangements are permitted because they reduce the fund's research cost

explanation.text: The Logic: The PFUTP-aligned discussion in the workbook makes clear that AIFs and distributors should not extend pass-backs (indirect incentives that induce subscriptions), managers should abstain from assuring returns, and sponsors should abstain from soft-dollar arrangements with distributors. The umbrella requirement is that AIFs and distributors observe high standards of ethics, integrity and fairness in all dealings, which is precisely what the keyed option states. The Trap: Options B, C and D try to legitimise practices that are treated as impermissible: pass-backs cannot be salvaged by PPM disclosure or by routing them only to Accredited Investors, and soft-dollar arrangements with distributors cannot be justified by characterising them as cost-saving on research. Note: Treat pass-backs, assured returns and soft-dollar arrangements with distributors as per-se impermissible conduct under the ethics/integrity/fairness umbrella; permissibility is not restored by disclosure, investor type, or business rationale.
